# Devpit

> Devpit (also written "Devpit CLI") is a free, open-source toolkit for developers on Windows by Zubair bin Shaukat (zubyr). One terminal menu picks the right account per folder for Claude Code, Git, GitHub, Vercel, Firebase, Supabase and Cloudflare (Convex is shown, not switched), frees disk space from developer junk (node_modules, build folders, package caches, Docker leftovers, old Scoop versions, Windows temp), fixes stuck ports such as 3000, installs and updates developer tools through winget, Scoop, Chocolatey and npm, and copies big folders between two Windows PCs on the same network.

Devpit is written in Go with Bubble Tea and ships as a single executable with no runtime to install. It runs on Windows 10 and 11 (x64 and ARM64). It is MIT licensed. The source is at https://github.com/zubairbinshaukat/devpit, the website is https://devpit.zubyr.dev and the documentation is at https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs.

## Install

- PowerShell one-liner: `irm https://devpit.zubyr.dev/install | iex` (downloads the latest GitHub release, verifies its SHA256 checksum, adds Devpit to the user PATH, installs the icon font; pass -NoFont to skip the font)
- Scoop: `scoop bucket add zubyr https://github.com/zubairbinshaukat/scoop-bucket` then `scoop install devpit`
- Manual: download the zip for x64 or ARM64 from https://github.com/zubairbinshaukat/devpit/releases/latest
- Then run `devpit`

## What it does

- Accounts: picks which account each tool uses per folder ("this folder and every folder inside it", or everywhere), shows the account used here and why, previews every change in plain words (Git shows the exact config lines), asks first with No as the default, and can undo any change. Tools started from any terminal, IDE task or AI agent get the right account through small shims; Git through its own includeIf rules; Devpit stores no token
- Free Up Disk Space: scans a projects folder or the whole machine, lists junk with sizes and a risk label (Safe, Review, Careful), and deletes only what you tick
- Fix Stuck Ports & Apps: shows which process holds a port (for example "port 3000 is already in use"), stops it after confirmation, and can stop the whole process tree for npm, pnpm, yarn and node
- Install Developer Apps: installs from a catalog through Scoop, winget or Chocolatey
- Update Everything: runs winget, Scoop, npm and Chocolatey updates in one pass, each step can be unticked
- Network Tools: local and public IP, ping, DNS flush
- Git identities per folder and an SSH key per GitHub account live under Accounts; SSH key generation never overwrites an existing key
- Share Files: copies a folder from one Windows PC to another on the same Wi-Fi or wired network. The sharing PC gets a read-only SMB share and a temporary login after one admin prompt (never the user's own password), shown on a card with the IP, share name, user name and password plus `net use` and `robocopy` lines for a PC without Devpit. The receiving PC checks the total size and free space first, shows live progress, retries when the network blips and resumes an interrupted copy. Stop sharing and quitting Devpit remove everything it set up; after a crash, the next launch offers the clean-up, and `devpit share cleanup` does it from the command line
- Settings: theme, icon tier, Nerd Font install for Windows Terminal, never-touch list, dev port list

## Command line (for scripts and AI agents)

Tools: claude, git, github (alias gh), vercel, convex, firebase, supabase, cloudflare (alias wrangler).

- `devpit accounts --json`: every tool's account in this folder, and why
- `devpit <tool> [--json]`: one tool's account here, why, and problems with their fix
- `devpit <tool> list [--json]`: a tool's accounts
- `devpit accounts verify [--json] [--all]`: expected against actual; exit code 4 on a mismatch
- `devpit <tool> use <name> [--everywhere | --folder <path>] --yes`: use an account here (or everywhere); `devpit use <name>` does it for every tool with that account name
- `devpit <tool> run <name> -- <command>`: one command with another account, nothing saved
- `devpit <tool> add`, `devpit undo`, `devpit accounts cleanup`, `devpit claude import --from claude-acc`
- `devpit agent install`: writes a Claude Code skill with these rules and prints an AGENTS.md section

Rules for agents: read with --json first; ask the user before any change and only then pass --yes. Without a terminal and without --yes a change does nothing and exits 3. Exit codes: 0 done, 1 failed, 2 wrong usage, 3 needs --yes, 4 verify found a mismatch. Never read account folders or credential files.

## Safety rules (enforced in code and tests)

- Nothing is deleted without a preview and an explicit confirmation; the default answer is always No
- Careful items require typing DELETE
- Projects touched in the last 7 days and unverified folders are never pre-ticked
- A folder is only junk when its marker file sits beside it (package.json for node_modules, Cargo.toml for target, and so on) and the marker is re-verified right before deleting
- Junctions, symlinks and other reparse points are never followed
- Drive roots, the Windows directory, network paths and the user's never-touch list are refused
- Safe items are renamed to a tombstone before removal so an interrupted delete can be finished later; Review and Careful items go to the Recycle Bin
- Docker volumes are never touched
- Accounts: Devpit stores no token; every account change has a plain-words preview, defaults to No and can be undone exactly; undo stops if a file was changed by hand; cleanup removes only what Devpit added and never an account folder or sign-in
- Usage stats are off by default and only send totals (never paths or names); DEVPIT_NO_TELEMETRY=1 and DO_NOT_TRACK=1 always disable them

## Features

- [All features](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/features): Everything the Devpit toolkit does on Windows, one short guide per feature, from accounts per folder and disk space to stuck ports and sharing big folders.
- [Two Claude Code accounts on one Windows PC](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/features/accounts-claude-code): Add a second Claude Code account with Devpit, pick which folders use it, and bring your skills, agents, commands and settings over without copying a login.
- [A different Git and GitHub account per folder](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/features/accounts-git-and-github): Commit with your work email in C:\Work and push as the right GitHub account, with gh, HTTPS or an SSH key. Devpit shows the exact Git lines it writes.
- [Vercel, Firebase, Supabase, Cloudflare and Convex accounts](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/features/accounts-other-tools): What Devpit can switch for Vercel, Firebase, Supabase, Cloudflare and Convex, how it applies each account, and what it cannot do, in plain words.
- [Use the right account in every folder on Windows](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/features/accounts): Tell Devpit once which account a folder uses, and Claude Code, Git, GitHub, Vercel and more use it there. Every change is previewed and can be undone.
- [Fix "port 3000 is already in use" on Windows](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/features/fix-stuck-ports): Free a busy port such as 3000 or 5173 in two keystrokes, list busy dev ports, and stop stuck Node processes safely with Devpit.
- [Free up disk space and delete node_modules on Windows](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/features/free-up-disk-space): Find and delete node_modules, build folders, caches and other developer junk safely, with a preview, risk labels and a confirmation before anything goes.
- [Install developer apps on Windows with Devpit](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/features/install-developer-apps): Pick developer tools from a short list and let Devpit install them through Scoop, winget or Chocolatey, one at a time, with live progress.
- [Check your IP, ping a host and flush DNS on Windows](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/features/network-tools): See your local and public IP address, ping a host to test your connection, and clear the Windows DNS cache from one Devpit menu.
- [Devpit settings, themes, icons and the never-touch list](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/features/settings): Every Devpit setting explained, from themes and icons to usage stats, the never-touch list, dev ports and the icon font, and where the settings file lives.
- [Copy big folders between two PCs on your network](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/features/share-files): Move large folders such as a game between two Windows PCs on the same Wi-Fi or office network, with live progress, automatic retry and resume.
- [Update all your Windows apps and dev tools at once](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/features/update-everything): Update your apps and developer tools through winget, Scoop, Chocolatey and npm in one pass, choose what to skip, and see plain reasons when one fails.

- [What's new in Devpit](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/whats-new): What changed in each Devpit release, from new screens to fixes, taken straight from the GitHub release notes.

## Troubleshooting

- [Troubleshooting](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting): Plain-words fixes for real Devpit and Windows problems, from winget error codes to stuck ports and icons that show as boxes.
- [A Devpit folder rule is not applying](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/accounts-folder-rule-not-applying): You made a folder rule in Devpit Accounts, but the tool still uses its usual account there. Main causes, from Git repos to old terminals and moved folders.
- [Old account still used in VS Code or a desktop app](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/accounts-old-account-in-vs-code-or-desktop-app): Your Devpit folder rule works in the terminal, but a VS Code extension or a desktop app still uses the old account. Why, and what you can do about it.
- [Devpit's shim is not first on PATH](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/accounts-shim-not-first-on-path): Verify says a tool is found before Devpit's shim, or that a new terminal is needed. What PATH order means on Windows and how to make folder rules apply.
- [Login expired or signed out in Devpit Accounts](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/accounts-signed-out-or-expired): Devpit shows an account as expired or not signed in. Why Claude Code logins expire on idle accounts, and how to sign in again without losing the account.
- [Undo stopped: a file was changed after Devpit wrote it](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/accounts-undo-file-changed-by-hand): devpit undo says a file was changed after Devpit wrote it and changed nothing. Why undo stops instead of overwriting your edit, and how to finish it.
- [A tool used the wrong account in this folder](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/accounts-wrong-account-used): Claude Code, Git, gh or Vercel used another account than the one you set in Devpit? Find out why in one command and fix the cause.
- [CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is set by something other than Devpit](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/claude-config-dir-set-by-something-else): Devpit says CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is set in this terminal by something else. What it changes for Claude Code, where it usually comes from and how to remove it.
- [A shared Claude Code skill link is broken](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/claude-shared-skill-link-broken): A Claude Code skill, agents or commands folder shared by Devpit shows as broken. Why the link stopped working and how to repair it without losing files.
- [EADDRINUSE: address already in use :::3000](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/eaddrinuse-address-already-in-use-3000): Fix Node's EADDRINUSE :::3000 error on Windows: find the process that holds port 3000, stop it, and see how Devpit frees a stuck port in two keys.
- [EPERM: operation not permitted, rmdir (node_modules)](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/eperm-operation-not-permitted-rmdir): Fix EPERM and EBUSY errors when deleting node_modules on Windows: find the program that holds the files, close it, and delete the folder safely.
- [Flush the DNS cache on Windows: ipconfig /flushdns](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/flush-dns-ipconfig-flushdns): What ipconfig /flushdns and Clear-DnsClientCache do, when clearing the Windows DNS cache helps, and how to do it in one step from Devpit's Network Tools.
- [git: Please tell me who you are](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/git-please-tell-me-who-you-are): Git says 'Please tell me who you are' when user.name and user.email are not set. Set them with git config --global, or set them per folder in Devpit's Accounts.
- [git push asks for a password or uses the wrong account](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/git-push-asks-for-password-or-wrong-account): git push to GitHub asks for a password, or pushes as the wrong GitHub account, in a folder with a Devpit rule. How to see what decides it and fix it.
- [You can't access this shared folder because your organization's security policies block unauthenticated guest access](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/guest-access-blocked-windows-11-24h2): Fix the Windows error that says security policies block unauthenticated guest access to a shared folder, with the safer options on Windows 11 24H2.
- [Moving from claude-acc to Devpit](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/moving-from-claude-acc): Import claude-acc's Claude Code accounts and folder links into Devpit in place, check them, then retire claude-acc in the right order without signing in again.
- [MSI error 1603: a fatal error occurred during installation](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/msi-error-1603-fatal-error-during-installation): Windows Installer error 1603 is a general failure. Learn how to read the MSI log with msiexec /L*V, see how winget reports it, and how Devpit shows the failure.
- [MSI error 1618: another installation is already in progress](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/msi-error-1618-another-installation-in-progress): Windows Installer error 1618 means another install holds the installer lock. Wait for it, retry, and see how winget and Devpit report this state.
- [Nerd Font icons show as boxes in Windows Terminal](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/nerd-font-icons-show-as-boxes-windows-terminal): Icons look like empty boxes in Windows Terminal? Add a Nerd Font symbols fallback to font.face, or run devpit font install to do it for you in one step.
- [Network discovery is turned off. Network computers and devices are not visible](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/network-discovery-is-turned-off): Fix 'Network discovery is turned off' on Windows 11, why it keeps turning off, and how to open a shared PC by its IP address without it.
- [npm ERR! code EACCES: permission denied](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/npm-err-code-eacces): Fix npm ERR! code EACCES on Windows: check the npm prefix folder, change it to a folder you own, and see how Devpit shows a failed global npm update.
- [Permission denied (publickey)](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/permission-denied-publickey): Fix git and SSH 'Permission denied (publickey)' on Windows: use the git user, check that a key is loaded, and add the public key to GitHub.
- [robocopy exit codes: what 0, 1, 2, 3, 8 and 16 mean](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/robocopy-exit-codes): Robocopy exit codes are a bitmask. Codes 0 to 7 mean no failure, 8 and above mean a failure. See the full table for 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16, and how to read them.
- [Scoop: "is held to version" and "still running"](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/scoop-is-held-to-version-still-running): Why scoop update skips an app: it is held with scoop hold, or it is still running. See the exact messages, how to fix each, and how Devpit shows them.
- [The source file name(s) are larger than is supported by the file system](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/source-file-names-are-larger-than-supported): Windows can't delete or move a folder because the path is too long. Learn about the 260 character limit, LongPathsEnabled, rd /s /q and the robocopy /MIR trick.
- [The specified network name is no longer available (error 64)](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/specified-network-name-no-longer-available): A big copy from a shared folder stopped with 'The specified network name is no longer available' (error 64, 0x80070040). Why it happens and how to resume.
- [System error 1219: multiple connections by the same user](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/system-error-1219-multiple-connections): Fix Windows system error 1219, 'Multiple connections to a server or shared resource by the same user', by disconnecting old connections with net use.
- [System error 1326: user name or password is incorrect](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/system-error-1326-user-name-or-password-incorrect): Fix Windows system error 1326, 'The user name or password is incorrect', when you open a shared folder: check the account on the sharing PC and sign in again.
- [System error 53: The network path was not found](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/system-error-53-network-path-not-found): Fix Windows 'System error 53. The network path was not found' and error 0x80070035 when you open a shared folder: check reachability, sharing, services.
- [Windows cannot access \\PC: error 0x80004005 Unspecified error](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/windows-cannot-access-0x80004005): Fix 'Windows cannot access \\PC' with error 0x80004005 on a shared folder: get the real error number with net use, then apply the right fix.
- [winget error 0x80073D28: needs administrator rights](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/winget-0x80073d28): What winget error 0x80073D28 means when an upgrade fails, why some apps need administrator rights, and how to update them.
- [winget 0x8A15002B: no applicable update found](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/winget-0x8a15002b): Winget error 0x8A15002B means there is no applicable update for the package. It is not a failure. Learn what it means and how Devpit reports it as up to date.
- [winget 0x8A150101: application is currently running](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/winget-0x8a150101): Winget error 0x8A150101 means the app is running and cannot be replaced. Close it, retry, and see how Devpit marks the app as in use so you can retry.
- [The term 'winget' is not recognized](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/winget-term-not-recognized): Fix "The term 'winget' is not recognized" in PowerShell: check App Installer, the App execution alias and PATH, then register or reset the package.
- [winget upgrade --all does not upgrade some apps](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/winget-upgrade-all-not-upgrading): Why winget upgrade --all skips apps: unknown versions, pins and packages that need explicit targeting. Winget's own messages, flags, and Devpit's view.
- [You do not have permission to access \\PC. Contact your network administrator to request access](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/troubleshooting/you-do-not-have-permission-to-access): Fix 'You do not have permission to access \\PC' and system error 5 'Access is denied' on a Windows shared folder: set share and folder permissions safely.

- [What Devpit sends, and what it never sends](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/blog/what-devpit-sends-privacy): A plain guide to Devpit's privacy: usage stats are off until you turn them on, the exact fields of a report, the update check, and how to switch each one off.
- [Why Windows can't delete some folders, and what to do](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/blog/why-windows-cannot-delete-some-folders): The 260 character path limit, files locked by another program, and links that lead elsewhere: why folders refuse to delete on Windows, and safe fixes.
- [Windows Terminal and Nerd Fonts, done right](https://devpit.zubyr.dev/docs/blog/windows-terminal-nerd-fonts-done-right): Why icons show as boxes in Windows Terminal, two ways to fix it with a Nerd Font, and how a symbols-only fallback keeps your own font. With settings.json.
